proof_skeleton_nl: Fix an arbitrary real number x. The proof splits into three pieces: an equality statement and two bounds. The equality comes from the algebraic decomposition x = floor(x) + (x - floor(x)) together with the identification frac(x) = x - floor(x). The lower and upper bounds come from the standard floor inequalities floor(x) ≤ x and x < floor(x) + 1, translated into statements about x - floor(x), and then rewritten using frac(x) = x - floor(x). After proving the equality and both bounds for the arbitrary x, conjoin them and generalize to all real numbers.

steps.derives: Fix an arbitrary real number x and reduce the goal to proving the conjunction for this particular x.
steps.trivial_justification: Universal quantification is handled by introducing an arbitrary element.

steps.derives: For the fixed x, x = floor(x) + frac(x).
steps.trivial_justification: Use the algebraic identity from L6 and rewrite x - floor(x) as frac(x) using L3.
Use the nonnegativity of the floor remainder from L4 and rewrite the remainder as frac(x) via L3.
Use the upper bound on the floor remainder from L5 and rewrite the remainder as frac(x) via L3.

steps.derives: For the fixed x, 0 ≤ frac(x) ∧ frac(x) < 1.
steps.trivial_justification: This is direct conjunction introduction from the two bounds.

steps.derives: For the fixed x, x = floor(x) + frac(x) ∧ 0 ≤ frac(x) ∧ frac(x) < 1.
steps.trivial_justification: Conjoin the equality from A2 with the bounds from A5, using the standard right-associative shape of conjunctions.

steps.derives: For every real number x, x = floor(x) + frac(x) ∧ 0 ≤ frac(x) ∧ frac(x) < 1.
steps.trivial_justification: Since x was arbitrary, universal generalization yields the quantified theorem.
